plain: A breaking of a law or moral rule

webster.text: The act of passing over or beyond any law or rule of moral duty; the violation of a law or known principle of rectitude; breach of command.

example.quote: When I observed that the elections were not secured on proper principles, I had an idea of far more probable and extensive evils, secret mischiefs, and not so glaring transgressions, the exclusions of proper district elections, and of the choice by a majority.
example.cite: Letters from the Federal Farmer to the Republican, Letter XII, Jan. 12, 1788
